title: Who's Who
subtitle: The network of relationships and individual accountability: documents cross-referenced with actions.
intro: The Lagovsky case did not happen by itself — it was built by specific individuals making specific decisions. This section is divided into two layers: a network map of the relationships involved, and individual profiles where official records sit side by side with what actually happened. We are not asking anyone to take our word for it. Compare the documents.

items.desc:
S. V. Palkin: Vice-President of OZHPT, initiator of the ownership grab.
FEZ: The company at the centre of the dispute.
The issue: A control conflict that was converted into a criminal case.

Yu. M. Salikov: The investigator who opened the case in defiance of Supreme Court and court rulings prohibiting it.
Mitrokhina: The Deputy Prosecutor responsible for oversight.
Prokopenko: The Deputy Prosecutor-General who signed the key refusals.
International search via Interpol (Red Notice, 25 January 2025), extradition proceedings in Serbia, and international review mechanisms. CCF complaint under review since 28 October 2025.

items.name: S. V. Palkin
items.role: Vice-President of OZHPT; Director of the Technical Regulation Directorate at LLC TC EurazHolding.
items.doc: Career biography within the Russian Railways and Evraz corporate structures.
items.action: Sergei Valentinovich Palkin's career has been built in the Russian railway industry. He was among those who helped establish OZHPT and has worked on technical standards for rails, wheels and axle sets. Since 2012 he has served as Director of the Technical Regulation Directorate for Railway Products at LLC TC EurazHolding. A criminal complaint was filed on 14 September 2022 through his lawyer V. O. Trofimchuk. At that stage, Lagovsky's name did not appear anywhere in the case materials.

items.name: Yu. M. Salikov
items.role: Lieutenant Colonel of Justice; Senior Investigator for Especially Important Cases, 6th Section, Special Investigation Unit, Moscow Region Main Investigation Department, Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs.
items.doc: Search record (15.12.2022), inspection records (17.12.2022 and 03.11.2023) — all signed by Yu. M. Salikov.
items.action: The investigator who opened the case despite a direct Supreme Court prohibition on proceedings of this type; who carried out a search despite a court order barring it; who issued a wanted notice without legal grounds. He personally conducted the seizure at LLC Company for Valuation and Law (Zemlyanoy Val St., 64, Bldg 2, Office 412) and inspected the seized CRM disc.

items.name: Mitrokhina
items.doc: The defence's formal complaint ran to five pages: eight numbered grounds, each citing specific statutory violations and dates.
items.action: The official response was a single line: 'No violations found.' The gap between the volume of documented violations and the institutional response to them requires no further commentary.

items.name: Prokopenko
items.doc: The official reply cites a Constitutional Court ruling as the legal basis for refusing the complaint.
items.action: A direct quotation from that same Constitutional Court ruling contains wording that is the precise opposite of the formula used in Prokopenko's response.

summary: This section places each person's individual contribution on record. It shows how a version of events that contradicts the documentary facts is assembled — through selective omission and the systematic substitution of one meaning for another.
